'''Douglas Stuart Butterworth''' is a retired South African [[fisheries scientist]] and [[applied mathematician]]. He is professor emeritus of applied mathematics at the [[University of Cape Town]], where he is the director of the Marine Resource Assessment and Management (MARAM) research group. 

== Early life and education ==
Butterworth attended the Western Province Preparatory School in [[Cape Town]],<ref>{{Cite web |last=Maluleke |first=Sagwadi |date=2019-05-26 |title=Award by Emperor of Japan – Professor Emeritus Doug Butterworth (1959) |url=https://wpps-alumni.org.za/2019/05/26/award-by-emperor-of-japan-professor-emeritus-doug-butterworth-1959/ |access-date=2024-06-26 |website=WPPS Alumni |language=en-US}}</ref> and he matriculated from nearby [[Bishops Diocesan College]] in 1963.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2019-05-23 |title=Prof. Butterworth (1963G) Receives Japanese Honour for Saving Bluefin Tuna |url=https://www.odunion.com/news/ods-in-the-news/413/413-Prof-Butterworth-1963G-Receives-Japanese-Honour-for-Saving-Bluefin-Tuna |access-date=2024-06-26 |website=Bishops OD Alumni Network |language=en}}</ref> Trained as a [[physicist]], he holds an MSc from the [[University of Cape Town]] and a PhD in [[Elementary particle physics|fundamental particle physics]] from [[University College London]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Douglas Stuart Butterworth |url=https://www.thepresidency.gov.za/douglas-stuart-butterworth |access-date=25 June 2024 |website=Presidency of the Republic of South Africa}}</ref>

After his doctoral degree, he spent four months as an adjunct lecturer at the [[University of Natal]]. He returned to Cape Town in 1977 to work in [[applied mathematics]] for the Sea Fisheries Branch, unable to find a job in physics.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |last=Duvenage |first=Engela |date=2019-09-02 |title=The UCT prof who helped save the bluefin tuna |url=https://scibraai.co.za/the-uct-prof-who-helped-save-the-bluefin-tuna/ |access-date=2024-06-26 |website=SciBraai |language=en-US}}</ref> He became involved in fisheries research in 1979, when he advised a co-worker – marine biologist [[Peter B. Best|Peter Best]] – about techniques for survey-based marine mammal [[abundance estimation]]. With Best's support, he became increasingly engaged in the research that Best was engaged in for the [[International Whaling Commission]].<ref name=":1" />

== University of Cape Town ==
After two years at the Sea Fisheries Branch, Butterworth joined the Department of Mathematics and Applied Mathematics at the University of Cape Town.<ref name=":1" /> His focus was [[applied mathematics]] and he primarily taught [[biomathematics]] and [[environmental modelling]]. His most important research concerned [[Stock assessment|fisheries assessment]], [[fisheries management]], and related modelling.<ref name=":0" />

In particular, Butterworth is known for developing the so-called management procedure approach to fisheries regulation in the late 1980s and early 1990s.<ref>{{Cite web |date=21 May 2019 |title=UCT professor honoured by Emperor of Japan |url=http://www.news.uct.ac.za/article/-2019-05-21-uct-professor-honoured-by-emperor-of-japan |access-date=2024-06-26 |website=University of Cape Town |language=en}}</ref> The procedure originated in an informal competition undertaken by Butterworth and [[Andre Punt]], a PhD student, against foreign research groups; in the course of the competition, Butterworth and Punt devised the procedure by using [[feedback control]] to refine computer simulations for [[whaling]] quotas.<ref name=":1" /> The management procedure approach is extremely compatible with the [[precautionary principle]] advocated by the [[Earth Summit]].<ref name=":0" /> The approach was subsequently applied to calculate annual catch targets for [[South African hake]], sardine, anchovy, and [[rock lobster]],<ref>{{Cite web |date=2019-09-12 |title=Fishing industry demonstrates strong support for world-renowned professor |url=https://sadstia.co.za/fishing-industry-demonstrates-strong-support-for-world-renowned-professor/ |access-date=2024-06-26 |website=SADSTIA |language=en-ZA}}</ref> and it spread beyond South Africa: Butterworth has advised at least 12 other countries, as well as [[fishing industry]] associations and international bodies (among them the scientific committees of the [[United Nations Food and Agriculture Organization|United Nations Food and Agriculture Organisation]] and the [[CITES|Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species]]).<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" /> In total, he has written over 1,500 technical reports, in addition to some 250 academic publications.<ref name=":1" />

After he retired from teaching, Butterworth remained the director of the university's Marine Resource Assessment and Management (MARAM) research group.<ref name=":1" />

== Honours and awards ==
Butterworth is a fellow of the [[Royal Society of South Africa]].<ref name=":1" /> In October 2008, President [[Kgalema Motlanthe]] admitted him to the [[Order of Mapungubwe]],'''<ref>{{Cite web |date=3 November 2008 |title=National Orders for UCT four |url=http://www.news.uct.ac.za/article/-2008-11-03-national-orders-for-uct-four |access-date=2024-06-26 |website=University of Cape Town |language=en}}</ref>''' granting him the award in silver for, "His excellent contribution to the betterment of the environment and [[sustainability of fisheries]]."<ref name=":0" />

In September 2019, the [[Emperor of Japan]] admitted Butterworth to the [[Order of the Rising Sun|Order of the Rising Sun, Third Class]].<ref>{{Cite web |last= |date=2019-06-04 |title=Fisheries scientist wins prestigious award |url=https://www.worldfishing.net/fisheries-scientist-wins-prestigious-award/1175896.article |access-date=2024-06-26 |website=World Fishing |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last= |date=2019-09-12 |title=Accolade: Fishing Industry Honours Doug Butterworth |url=https://www.fishingindustrynewssa.com/2019/09/12/accolade-fishing-industry-honours-doug-butterworth/ |access-date=2024-06-26 |website=Fishing Industry News and Aquaculture SA |language=en-GB}}</ref> Having served on the Japanese delegation to the scientific committee of the [[Commission for the Conservation of Southern Bluefin Tuna]], he received the award for his contribution to the sustainable management of [[Fishing in Japan|Japan's marine resources]], particularly [[southern bluefin tuna]].<ref>{{Cite news |date=21 May 2019 |title=UCT scientist honoured for helping to save Japan's bluefin tuna |url=https://www.timeslive.co.za/news/south-africa/2019-05-21-uct-scientist-honoured-for-helping-to-save-japans-bluefin-tuna/ |access-date=25 June 2024 |work=Sunday Times}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |date=12 September 2019 |title=Japan honours UCT fisheries scientist Butterworth for 'distinguished achievements' |url=https://www.iol.co.za/capetimes/news/japan-honours-uct-fisheries-scientist-butterworth-for-distinguished-achievements-32862290 |access-date=25 June 2024 |work=Cape Times}}</ref>
